questions.question: In the factorisation $PA=LU$, what role does $P$ play?
options: It stores the upper triangular part.
It is always the zero matrix.
It is the right-hand side vector.

questions.question: In an LU decomposition, what kind of matrix is $L$?
In an LU decomposition, what kind of matrix is $U$?
What does LU decomposition record in matrix form?
options: The definition of a vector space.

questions.question: When can the factorisation be written as $A=LU$ instead of $PA=LU$?
options: Only when $A$ is the zero matrix.
When no row interchanges are needed.

questions.question: If $L=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\3&1\end{pmatrix}$ and $U=\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\0&4\end{pmatrix}$, what is $LU$?
If no row swaps are needed and $A=LU$, what is $P$ in the form $PA=LU$?
To solve $Ax=b$ from $A=LU$, which system is solved first?
If $PA=LU$ and $Ax=b$, what right-hand side appears after multiplying the equation by $P$?
Which pair of methods is naturally used after LU decomposition to solve a system?
options: Taking a trace followed by diagonalisation.
Finding a minor followed by row swapping only.
Forward substitution followed by back substitution.
Cofactor expansion followed by Sarrus' rule.

questions.question: Why does LU decomposition help when solving several systems with the same matrix $A$ but different right-hand sides?
options: The factorisation is reused; only triangular solves remain
It guarantees every right-hand side has the same solution.
The matrix $A$ no longer has to be multiplied by vectors.

questions.question: What is the point of allowing row permutations in $PA=LU$?
options: They remove the need for triangular matrices.
They handle pivoting when row interchanges are needed

questions.question: Why are triangular factors useful after decomposition?
options: Triangular matrices always have determinant zero.
They turn every equation into a polynomial equation.
Triangular systems can be solved step by step.

questions.question: Let $L=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\2&1\end{pmatrix}$ and $U=\begin{pmatrix}3&1\\0&2\end{pmatrix}$. What is $LU$?
Solve using $L=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\2&1\end{pmatrix}$ and $U=\begin{pmatrix}1&3\\0&2\end{pmatrix}$ with $LUx=\begin{pmatrix}5\\14\end{pmatrix}$. What is $x$?
Let $P=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$ and $b=\begin{pmatrix}7\\9\end{pmatrix}$. In $LUx=Pb$, what is $Pb$?
A student writes $A=LU$ even though a row swap was used during elimination. What is missing?
options: The right-hand side vector must be deleted.
The determinant of $A$ must be added to $L$.
A permutation matrix $P$ is needed, as in $PA=LU$

questions.question: Why is LU decomposition more than simply writing any matrix as a product of two matrices?
options: The factors are arbitrary and need not relate to $A$.
The factors have special triangular structure tied to elimination.
It only applies to scalar numbers.

questions.question: Suppose $PA=LU$, $\det(P)=-1$, $\det(L)=1$, and $\det(U)=6$. What is $\det(A)$?
For $A=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\2&3\end{pmatrix}$, why would pivoting be needed before a standard first elimination step?
options: The top-left pivot is $0$, so swap rows
